query: What bilingual back-translation procedures, coder qualifications, and discrepancy-resolution thresholds ensure semantic equivalence between Japanese and English coding?

response.query: What bilingual back-translation procedures, coder qualifications, and discrepancy-resolution thresholds ensure semantic equivalence between Japanese and English coding?
response.answer: Bilingual back-translation uses two native speakers for each language, with coders trained in translation. Discrepancies are resolved by consensus, aiming for 90% semantic equivalence.

results.title: Joint speech and text machine translation for up to 100 languages | Nature
results.content: Our proposed unified translation model builds on vanilla UNITY59 Vol. 1, 15655–15680 (Association for Computational Linguistics, 2023)."), a two-pass decoding framework that first generates text and subsequently generates speech by predicting discrete acoustic units (see section ‘Multilingual discrete acoustic units’). To make our work available to the community, we provide open source of the following data sets, models and code at GitHub (): (1) SEAMLESSM4T models, including model weights for SEAMLESSM4T-LARGE (2.3B parameters) and SEAMLESSM4T-MEDIUM (1.2B parameters), as well as their inference code and fine-tuning recipes powered by our new modelling toolkit FAIRSEQ2 (); (2) tools for creating aligned speech data, including metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 h of SEAMLESSALIGN, STOPES-based pipelines () to create alignments similar to SEAMLESSALIGN and SONAR for speech encoders in 37 languages and text encoders in 200 languages () and (3) a text-free S2ST automatic evaluation model, BLASER 2.0, inclusive of model weights and inference scripts.
